chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
Regarding a man who killed his father, he said: 'He does not inherit him. If the killer has a son, the son inherits the slain grandfather.'

key_terms.الْقَاتِلِ: The killer (specifically the heir who killed the deceased)
key_terms.وَرِثَ: He inherited (past tense, indicating the legal outcome for the grandson)
key_terms.يَرِثُهُ: He inherits him (referring to the killer inheriting the deceased)

ai.seo_question: Does a son who kills his father inherit from him, and what happens to the grandfather's estate?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific application of *hijr* (blocking) in inheritance, distinguishing between the killer's exclusion and the right of representation (*hukm al-walad al-asfal*) for his descendants. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that the killer is barred from inheriting the deceased directly, yet his son steps into his place to inherit the grandfather, preserving the lineage's share. This ruling underscores the principle that the defect of the killer does not extinguish the inheritance right of the next generation.
